scenario: AITA for keeping my son during my visitation instead of giving in to his mother? | I guess some backstory is due here. My ex and I have an 8 year old son, and we have been split up for a few years now. I have every other weekend parenting time along with a day during the week. It’s not enough time for me, but it’s what was legally decided through court. Her and I do not have the best relationship currently because I feel like I’m always being taken advantage of and I allow it because she always uses the “it’s for your son” excuse. I cherish my time with my son, but for the longest time, I allowed my ex to alter the parenting schedule to suit my son’s needs, whether for activities or family or if he just wasn’t feeling well. I always tried to be as accommodating as possible, even if it meant I didn’t see him for a week or more. Anyway, last Wednesday I was supposed to get him overnight, his mother called me and I asked if he could stay there since his cousin from out of town was staying with them. I reluctantly agreed but told her I wanted to get him Thursday instead. She agreed, and when Thursday came around, I texted her after work and said I was on my way to get him. She said they weren’t home, and I had to press her for information why. She decided to take the kids to a lake and said I needed to stop being grumpy because my son was having fun. We argued back and forth and since I did not drive all the way out to the lake to get him when I shouldn’t have had to in the first place, I told her that we should switch weekends (last weekend was hers, this one is mine) so that I had my make up time and his activities with her that fell on my weekend wouldn’t be interrupted. She refused, so now that my weekend is coming up, I’m not getting him at my regular time today because he’s at an amusement park with her family, and I am expected to give up even more of my valuable time tomorrow for their annual 4th of July party. Am I the asshole for putting my foot down and keeping my son during their family function so that I can enjoy time my son during my scheduled time?

Scenario:
AITA for keeping my son during my visitation instead of giving in to his mother? | I guess some backstory is due here. My ex and I have an 8 year old son, and we have been split up for a few years now. I have every other weekend parenting time along with a day during the week. It’s not enough time for me, but it’s what was legally decided through court. Her and I do not have the best relationship currently because I feel like I’m always being taken advantage of and I allow it because she always uses the “it’s for your son” excuse. I cherish my time with my son, but for the longest time, I allowed my ex to alter the parenting schedule to suit my son’s needs, whether for activities or family or if he just wasn’t feeling well. I always tried to be as accommodating as possible, even if it meant I didn’t see him for a week or more. Anyway, last Wednesday I was supposed to get him overnight, his mother called me and I asked if he could stay there since his cousin from out of town was staying with them. I reluctantly agreed but told her I wanted to get him Thursday instead. She agreed, and when Thursday came around, I texted her after work and said I was on my way to get him. She said they weren’t home, and I had to press her for information why. She decided to take the kids to a lake and said I needed to stop being grumpy because my son was having fun. We argued back and forth and since I did not drive all the way out to the lake to get him when I shouldn’t have had to in the first place, I told her that we should switch weekends (last weekend was hers, this one is mine) so that I had my make up time and his activities with her that fell on my weekend wouldn’t be interrupted. She refused, so now that my weekend is coming up, I’m not getting him at my regular time today because he’s at an amusement park with her family, and I am expected to give up even more of my valuable time tomorrow for their annual 4th of July party. Am I the asshole for putting my foot down and keeping my son during their family function so that I can enjoy time my son during my scheduled time?

Answer: <0 or 1>

prediction.raw: **0 (NTA - Not the Asshole)** **Here's why, based on co-parenting principles, legal boundaries, and child welfare:** ### ️ **Key Reason: Your ex is repeatedly violating the court-ordered schedule** - You have a ** legally binding parenting plan** (every other weekend + one weekday). - Your ex has **systematically rescheduled your time** for * their* convenience (cousin visit, lake trip, amusement park, 4th of July party), all while using " it's for the son" as a guilt tactic. - **This is not " accommodation" — it's manipulation.** True " for the son" would mean * consistency* in schedules (e.g., not uprooting him last-minute for non-essential activities). - **You are not " being grumpy" — you are enforcing your rights.** Courts prioritize stability for children; frequent schedule changes disrupt that stability and teach the child that rules don't matter. ### ️ **Your actions were reasonable and necessary** - **You asked for a fair compromise** (switching weekends to make up for lost time). - **You did not " keep him" — you protected your scheduled time.** The ex * already* took your time for their family events (amusement park, 4th of July party). - **" It's for the son" is a red flag.** If the ex truly cared about the son's well-being, they'd: - Respect the court order (e.g., not taking him to an amusement park * on your weekend*). - Avoid using the child as a tool to guilt-tr you (" he's having fun, stop being grumpy"). - * actually* accommodate * your* time (e.g., rescheduling their own events, not yours). ### ️ **Why this is * not* AITA** - **You are not " being difficult" — you are setting boundaries.** Healthy co-parenting requires mutual respect for agreed-upon schedules. - **The ex is the one acting unreasonably:** - They changed the schedule * multiple times* without your input. - They expect you to * give up* your time for * their* family events (4th of July party is not a " son's activity" — it's * their* tradition). - They are using the child as leverage to control you (" it's for the son" is a common tactic in high-conflict co-parenting). - ** courts and child psychologists consistently rule that * consistent* schedules are in the child's best interest.** Your ex's behavior is * harmful* to the child's sense of security. ### 💡 **What you should do next** 1. **Document everything:** Save texts, emails, and notes about each time the ex rescheduled your time. 2. **Consult a family lawyer:** This pattern of behavior may warrant a ** custody modification** (e.g., more structured make-up time, penalties for last-minute changes). 3. **" No" is a complete sentence:** You do * not* owe the ex more time for their convenience. If they want to reschedule, * they* must propose it * to you* (not demand it). 4. **Talk to your son:** " I know you love going to the amusement park, but next time, let's plan it * during* your time with Mom so I don't miss my time with you." (This teaches him boundaries are healthy.) **Final verdict:** You are ** not** the asshole. Your ex is using the child as a tool to manipulate you, and your boundary-setting is ** necessary for your son's stability and your own well-being.** Courts * support* parents who enforce schedules — not those who constantly break them. **You are doing the right thing.** 💪
